body.name: recursive task-elimination and district-splitting transition
body.construction: Write \(\zeta\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{elim}}\zeta'\) for the operation produced by the compiler in one of its nonfixing recursive cases. An ancestor operation replaces \((G_\tau,q_\tau,Y_\tau,X_\tau)\) by the induced ancestor task and the exact marginal kernel \(\sum_{R_\tau\setminus\operatorname{an}(Y_\tau)}q_\tau\). An intervention-augmentation operation removes the computed nonempty nonancestor set from the active random mask. A district operation computes all districts of the current postintervention graph and replaces one parent task by the canonically ordered child tasks, each on a strict subset of the parent's active mask. A terminal operation removes the completed task and appends its required marginal or ambient-district factor to the accumulated projection circuit. Every operation is admitted only after expanding and checking its finite polynomial identity modulo \(\mathcal J\). After cancelling common factors and normalizing signs, every new denominator is registered only in its explicitly computed form as a positive rational constant times earlier ledger entries and nonempty sums of branch-reachable positive kernel cells.
